paragraphs.text: Danny: I hope it’s clay today.
Brad: You always hope it’s clay.
Danny: Modeling clay is the best!
Tina: I wish it were gym class.
Mr. Smith: Children, please. Please sit down.
Danny: I hope it’s clay. Please, I hope it’s clay.
Mr. Smith: Today, for art class we will be using . . .
Danny: CLAY?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Danny, we’re using clay. Not so loud next time.
Danny: Sorry.
Brad: You’re always so excited!
Danny: Shh. I don’t want to get into more trouble!
Mr. Smith: Here you go, Tina.
Tina: I just want black and white please.
Mr. Smith: Why is that, Tina?
Tina: Well, those are the colors of a soccer ball.
Brad: Actually, black isn’t really a color.
Mr. Smith: Very good, Brad. Black is really no color at all.
Danny: How did you know that?
Brad: My computer has all the answers.
Mr. Smith: Children, I’m handing out seven colors because . . .
Danny: Who’s this guy Roy?
Mr. Smith: Well, if you’d let me explain . . .
Danny: Is he a new kid in class?
Mr. Smith: No, Danny, Roy G. Biv is . . . A cloud. It must have been a cloud.
Danny: Who is Roy G. Biv?
Mr. Smith: Yes. That’s what I was saying. Roy G. Biv stands for . . .
Tina: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue . . .
Brad: I knew that.
Mr. Smith: Very good, Tina. Keep going.
Tina: Well, those are the colors in front of me.
Mr. Smith: Brad, do you know the rest?
Brad: Indigo and violet. The colors of the rainbow.
Mr. Smith: Very good, Brad!
Danny: Can we start? My imagination is going crazy!!
Mr. Smith: Danny, it’s not nice to interrupt. Class, you may now begin. Create whatever you want.
Tina: What are you doing?
Danny: I’m just looking.
Tina: At what?
Danny: What are you making? Is it a tree?
Tina: It’s going to be a soccer player.
Danny: That gives me an idea!
Brad: How’s it going over there, Mr. Artist?
Danny: I don’t think I’ve got it right yet.
Mr. Smith: Danny, more art and less talk.
Danny: But when I talk, it helps my hands move!
Mr. Smith: Danny, don’t bother the other students.
Tina: You’re going to get into trouble.
Danny: I need to look at you more closely.
Tina: What are you talking about?
Danny: Come here and look! See?
Tina: That’s pretty good, Danny.
Danny: Yeah, but I’m missing something.
Brad: She’s right. That looks good, Danny.
Dave: Hey! Look at this!
Chuck: Well, well, well. Isn’t this cute!
Danny: Just leave me alone.
Chuck: Aww. He likes the girl!
Dave: He’s in love with her.
Chuck: Are you guys going to get married?
Danny: Give me that!
Dave: He wants his girlfriend back.
Danny: She’s not my girlfriend! Stop! You’re squishing my model!
Tina: Why don’t you leave him alone?
Chuck: Isn’t that sweet? She's standing up for her boyfriend.
Tina: You don’t want to make me angry.
Dave: Why? What’s going to happen?
Tina: Have you forgotten what happened last week?
Chuck: Here’s your little doll back!
Dave: You’re lucky that your girlfriend is strong.
Danny: SHE’S NOT MY GIRLFRIEND!
Tina: Danny, quiet.
Mr. Smith: What’s going on here? Why are you yelling, Danny?
Danny: These guys are driving me crazy!
Mr. Smith: Danny, I think you’re driving me crazy.
Tina: No, really, Mr. Smith. These boys were picking on Danny.
Mr. Smith: Is that true, boys?
Dave: No, Mr. Smith.
Chuck: We just like his clay models.
Dave: Yeah. We think they’re really good.
Mr. Smith: Danny? What do you have to say?
Danny: They . . . are . . . big . . . stinking . . . LIARS!
Mr. Smith: Danny, that’s enough!
Tina: Danny, calm down.
Brad: Mr. Smith?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Brad.
Brad: I can prove that Danny is innocent.
Mr. Smith: Brad, please return to your desk. Everybody, back to your desks.
Danny: But Mr. Smith. . .
Mr. Smith: That’s enough, Danny. We will not be using clay anymore today!
Mr. Smith: Please pull out your workbooks.
Tina: Sorry, Danny.
Dave: We’ll see you at recess, Danny.
Danny: No more clay?
Mr. Smith: Now, Danny . . .
Danny: Yes, Mr. Smith?
Mr. Smith: You can’t yell in class.
Danny: But they were being mean to me!
Mr. Smith: Danny . . .
Danny: They’re bullies!
Mr. Smith: You were the one making all the noise.
Danny: I’m just an excited guy!
Mr. Smith: Danny, please throw out your clay.
Danny: I don’t want to.
Mr. Smith: Please do it now. Thank you. Now, go sit in the corner until recess.
Danny: Please! I promise to be quiet!
Mr. Smith: No. You’ll sit there and think about what you’ve done.
Danny: Do I have to?
Mr. Smith: Yes, Danny. You do.
Brad: I thought your models looked good, Danny.
Danny: Thanks. They’re garbage now.
Tina: You tried to stand up to those bullies. Good for you.
Danny: But now I’m in trouble.
Dave: Ha-ha!
Chuck: Ha-ha!
Danny: It’s not fair.
Mr. Smith: Now, Danny, I want you to put your head on the desk. And think about what you did.
Danny: I was making great art, but . . .
Mr. Smith: What’s the lesson, Danny?
Danny: I don’t know.
Mr. Smith: You shouldn’t get so excited in the future.
Danny: I’ve got a great imagination! I can’t help it!
Mr. Smith: Okay, class. Turn to page six in your books.
Chuck: Hey, Danny. I’ll save that little doll you made.
Danny: Leave me alone.
Chuck: Then you can have it forever.
Danny: Dumb people are always getting me into trouble . . . I just wanted to play with my clay. That’s all. Who’s that?
Danny: Who are you?
Hopian: It’s all right. There’s nothing to be afraid of.
Danny: What are you doing here?
Hopian: My name is Hopian, Danny.
Danny: How do you know my name?
Hopian: I’ve been watching you.
Danny: Watching me? Why?

Hopian: Only you can help us, Danny. I come from Ginormous. It’s a land filled with giants like myself. The people of Ginormous were usually very happy. We all got along with each other. We knew how to play. Families used to gather for picnics in the colorful gardens. The giant children used to sing and paint pictures. My son used to make clay castles.
Danny: Sounds like fun! What happened?
Hopian: Our color is disappearing, Danny.
Danny: What do you mean?

Hopian: I noticed it about a month ago.I went outside one day to get ready for a party. Our friends and neighbors were going to join us. I looked around the garden, and then I noticed something. I walked up to a plant that was normally bright blue. But now it was gray! I bent down to look at the grass. I noticed that it had faded too. I was surprised, and started to feel sad.
Danny: That’s terrible!

Hopian: As the weeks passed, I noticed more and more gray. My friends were no longer very happy. People seemed to change.Something evil is happening to my world. My people are very sad. They miss color. That’s why I came to you.
Danny: Why me?
Hopian: Everyone in Ginormous is forgetting all about color. But you still have a colorful imagination.
Danny: But what can I do? I’m just a little kid.
Hopian: I brought something for you, Danny. It came from my world.
Danny: That’s so cool!
Hopian: It’s beautiful, isn’t it?
Danny: But I thought all the color was gone from your world!

Hopian: So did I. But I found something the other day. I have a young son named Bello. He is two years old. When I came home the other day, he looked happy. He was running around with a big smile. I guessed something was going on. He led me into his room. He took some clay from under his bed. He started making a circus with it. There were big blue horses, a large red tent, and a funny yellow clown. Bello laughed. His eyes were shining. Then I noticed something. His beautiful fur was shining with color! I realized that Bello’s imagination was giving him color. I was so happy that I cried. I took his clay into my hands and closed my eyes. I wondered how this little bit of clay could help. When I opened my eyes, I was outside your classroom.
Danny: The clay led you to me?
Hopian: My imagination led me to you. Your ability with clay will heal our world. It will be a colorful, happy place again.
Danny: I don’t know how to do that!
Hopian: I know you can do it, Danny.
Danny: But you haven’t told me how!
Hopian: Danny, I can’t stay here any longer. I have to go now. But I’m going to leave this clay with you. Look for it in your desk.
Danny: Hopian, don’t go!
Hopian: Danny, use your imagination. Find your way to Ginormous. Once you’re there, I’ll help you any way I can.
Danny: But I have no idea where Ginormous is! How can I get there?
Hopian: Remember, your imagination can unlock any door. Good-bye, Danny. I know I’ll see you soon.
Danny: Hopian!
Hopian: Your imagination can unlock any . . .
Brad: It’s recess time.
Tina: Is everything okay?
Brad: Yeah, you were making strange noises. We saw you moving like a jumping bean.
Danny: You didn’t see him?
Tina & Brad: See who?
Danny: Well, I saw him and I know he’s real!
Brad: Who’s real?
Danny: Aha! It’s here! He left the clay for me.
Tina: Danny, you’re acting really weird.
Danny: Let’s go! Follow me to our secret place! Hurry! You guys have to listen to me.
Tina: Okay.
Danny: And believe me.
Brad: Well, that depends on what you say.
Danny: Okay. I just had a visit.
Brad: You were asleep at your desk.
Danny: No, no. Just listen─
Brad: Well, you’re not making any sense.
Tina: Brad, just listen to Danny.
Danny: Thank you. My visitor was a giant named Hopian. We have to go to his world. It’s called Ginormous. We have to bring back the lost color to his world.
Tina: That’s a good one, Danny!
Brad: And you were so serious the whole time!
Tina: A giant!
Brad: Bring back the lost color!
Danny: I’m serious!
Brad: Danny, you had a dream about art class. That’s all.
Tina: You have got the wildest imagination.
Danny: That’s what Hopian said!
Tina: Sorry, Danny. But I’d rather play soccer than listen to this.
Danny: No, I’ve got proof. Hopian gave me something.
Brad: A map to his magic giant land?
Danny: No. I wish it was a map, though. Here.
Brad: What’s that?
Danny: It’s clay from Hopian’s world. It’s going to help us get there.
Brad: That’s just the clay from art class.
Tina: This clay is glowing, Brad. That clay didn’t glow.
Danny: What is it?
Brad: This clay is not from our world.
Tina: What do you mean, "It’s not from this world"?
Brad: It’s not from this world. I checked the Internet. We don’t have clay like that.
Danny: I told you I was telling the truth!
Tina: So this clay was given to you . . . by a giant?
Danny: I told you his name is Hopian.
Brad: And what are you supposed to do?
Danny: We’re supposed to help bring back the lost color to his world!
Tina: And how are we going to do this?
Danny: He told me to remember something. He said, "Your imagination can unlock any door."
Tina: Your imagination?
Danny: Yes.
Brad: Can unlock any door?
Danny: Yes.
Brad: What does that mean?
Danny: I don’t know!
Tina: This is crazy.
Brad: Wait a second. It’s got to be some sort of riddle.
Tina: And?
Brad: My computer can solve any problem.
Danny: So what does it say?
Brad: Maybe I’m not putting it in right.
Tina: Any answer is better than nothing. What does it say?
Brad: "Every door is different."
Tina: Hey, I’ve got an idea. Maybe if we look at it long enough, we’ll figure it out.
Brad: I can barely read that.
Tina: You know what it says!
Danny: Hey, don’t fight. Maybe it’s up to me.
Tina: He did say, "Your imagination."
Brad: And you have this special clay to help. Right?
Danny: That’s it!
Tina: What’s it?
Danny: Stand back and watch!
Brad: Oh great. Who are you? Harry Potter?
Danny: ALA KAZAAM KABLAM , TAKE ME TO GINORMOUS!
Brad: Um . . . didn’t work.
Tina: We’re still in the bushes, Danny.
Danny: My imagination isn’t that great, I guess.
Brad: Only two more minutes of recess left!
Tina: Yeah, we don’t want to be late. Let’s go!
Danny: What’s that sound?
Tina: It’s just my keys. Hurry!
Danny: WAIT!
Brad: Come on, Danny!
Danny: I’ve got it. Keys!
Tina: Keys?
Danny: Yes. Oh, don’t you see?
Brad: All I can see is that we’re going to be late.
Danny: Just one second! There! See, your imagination will unlock the door. What unlocks doors? Keys!
Tina: We’ve got to go, Danny.
Brad: Let’s try to figure this out after school, okay?
Danny: There’s no time.
Tina: Danny, what are you doing?
Brad: I’ve never been in trouble at school before.
Danny: My imagination will unlock the door . . .
Tina: What’s that?
Brad: A cloud. But it’s acting very strange.
Danny: Did it work?
Tina: Only If you imagined rain.
Brad: Strange, very strange.
Danny: Look!
Tina: Wow.
Brad: I knew that cloud looked strange.
Danny: Let’s go!
Brad: Wait, Danny! What if there are monsters behind there?
Tina: Or what if we can’t find our way home again?
Danny: Look, Hopian is a good giant. He needs our help. Their whole world needs our help. We can’t let him down!
Tina: He’s right, Brad. We can’t just stand by and do nothing. I’m with you, Danny.
Brad: Okay. Me too.
Danny: Hello? Hopian? This isn’t how I pictured Ginormous. Maybe we came to the wrong place.
Brad: I think we should go back and try again.
Tina: I don’t think we’re going anywhere, guys.
Danny: Why not?
Tina: Because the door has disappeared!
Brad: But the door was right there!
Tina: I know where it was.
Danny: How is that possible?
Brad: We’re doomed!
Tina: Now, let’s not get scared.
Danny: Why not?
Tina: Because if there’s a way in, there’s got to be a way out.
Brad: Let me ask my computer!
Danny: Well?
Brad: I asked it, "What’s the best way to get out?"
Danny: And what did it say?
Brad: It said, "Find an exit."
Danny: That computer is useless!
Tina: Danny, calm down.
Brad: She’s right. Getting upset won’t help.
Danny: Well, being calm isn’t helping.
Tina: It’s as if we’re in the woods.
Brad: Lost in the woods, that’s us.
Danny: I can make a compass!
Tina: What?
Danny: A compass! We find out which direction to go with a compass. There, that way is north.
Brad: What good does that do?
Danny: Well . . .
Tina: If we keep walking in one direction, I’m sure we’ll find something.
Danny: She’s right. Standing here won’t help.
Brad: Something feels funny.
Danny: Yeah, the ground is all squishy.
Tina: My shoes are getting wet.
Brad: Yeah. Mine too.
Tina: The ground is getting squishier!
Brad: Our feet are sinking in.
Danny: Whoa!
Brad: You must have stepped on a geyser!
Tina: Look at that!
Danny: Our footsteps are making puddles.
Brad: This isn’t good!
Tina: Let’s start running!
Danny: I can’t get my feet out!
Brad: This is really bad!
Tina: I wish I were a giant so I could just leap out of this.
Brad: If you were a giant, you’d just sink faster.
Danny: What are we going to do?
Tina: Look! Over there! We’re saved!
Danny: How are we saved?
Tina: We just need to get over there, to higher ground.
Brad: I wish your friend Hopian was here. He could tell us what to do!
Danny: Ha-ha!
Brad: What are you so happy about?
Danny: Hopian already told me what to do!
Brad: What was it?
Danny: Imagination is the key, remember?
Tina: So, how do we imagine our way over to the trees?
Danny: I guess. . .
Brad: I’ve got it! Think light thoughts!
Danny: What do you mean?
Brad: Think of the lightest thing you can. Imagine that you're a feather or something.
Tina: It might work.
Brad: Let me test it out.
Tina: It’s working!
Brad: I made it! I made it! We’re going to be safe.
Danny: What did you think of?
Brad: Marshmallows! I imagined that my feet were marshmallows!
Danny: Now I’m hungry.
Tina: It’s my turn!
Brad: Good job! Keep going!
Tina: That was easy. Great idea, Brad! It really works.
Brad: Come on, Danny. Your turn.
Danny: This’ll be easy!
Tina: He’ll be here in no time! You’re really smart, Brad.
Brad: Yeah. I didn’t even need my computer this time.
Tina: Oh no!
Brad: Danny! What’s happening?
Danny: I was thinking of a balloon. Then I started to think of a baboon instead!
Brad: Concentrate on the balloon!
Danny: I’m trying!
Brad: Let’s help him.
Brad & Tina: Balloon, balloon, balloon, balloon. . . Good job, Danny!
Brad: Okay, now that we’re safe up here, where do we go?
Tina: Maybe we can swim?
Brad: We can’t swim through soggy land. Besides, where would we swim to?
Danny: Hey, maybe if we imagine the giants’ world, we will appear there!
Danny: Okay, imagine Ginormous on the count of three. Ready? One, two, three!
Brad: I don’t think this is working.
Danny: You’re both imagining Ginormous, right?
Tina: Yes, a world full of giants playing.
Brad: A giant world without color.
Danny: I don’t think you guys are picturing it right.
Tina: How can we imagine a place we’ve never seen?
Danny: You’re right. But how else are we going to get out of here! Ow!
Brad: What was that?
Danny: That was the sound of my foot on that tree!
Tina: The tree made a funny sound when you kicked it.
Brad: Not funny, hollow.
Danny: But trees aren’t hollow.
Brad: This one is.
Tina: A hollow tree!
Danny: What is it made of?
Brad: It looks like some kind of aluminum, just like a can.
Tina: How is it growing then?
Brad: I don’t think this tree has any roots.
Danny: It’s definitely not a real tree. It was put here, not planted.
Brad: There might be something interesting underneath it.
Danny: How can we get it up?
Tina: The ground is too wet to dig. The holes just keep filling up with water.
Brad: Hey, guys?
Danny: What?
Brad: Danny, Tina. Come and stand in a circle around the tree. Okay, hold on tight to the tree, and when I say go, everyone, walk to the right. Ready? Go!
Danny: Brad! The tree is moving!
Brad: Just as I thought, the tree is screwed into the ground. And it’s made of aluminum, so it 's pretty light. I think we can lift it.
Tina: Way to go, Brad!
Danny: Let’s get this tree out of here!
Brad: What’s down there?
Tina: I don’t know, but it’s dark and wet.
Brad: More water is the last thing we need!
Danny: Well, I think it looks safe.
Tina: I wonder what would happen if we jumped in.
Brad: That’s my point. We don’t know what might happen!
Danny: Hey! It feels smooth, just like a waterslide.
Tina: A waterslide! They are so much fun.
Brad: You’re both crazy. You don’t know where it leads.
Danny: It has to lead somewhere. I think we should try it.
Tina: I’ll go first! Ready? Start right after me, Brad!
Danny: You better go, Brad. We don’t want to lose her. One, two, three! I’m right behind you!
Tina: Wheee! This is incredible!
Brad: I think I’m going to be sick.
Danny: This is more fun than being in class!
Brad: Whoo-hoo!
Danny: That’s the spirit, Brad.
Tina: It’s about time we had fun!
Danny: Which way do we go?
Tina: I don’t know! Brad, what do you think?
Brad: How should I know?!
Danny: Somebody decide quickly!
Tina: This way!
Brad: What if we went the wrong way?
Tina: Then this won’t be much fun anymore.
Danny: We haven’t done too badly, so far.
Brad: Oh yeah? Well, just look ahead.
Al threel: Aaah!
Tina: Danny . . . this isn’t good.
Brad: Yeah. Now would be a good time to use your imagination again.
Danny: I’ve got an idea! Hold on to me!
Brad: What?
Danny: You and Tina. Hold on to me!
Tina: This better work!
Brad: Oh no!
Tina: Danny, do something!
Danny: Both of you, start blowing.
Tina: You’re a genius, Danny!
Brad: Hey, I’m the smart one.
Danny: More blowing, less talking! That’s it, I think we’ve stopped falling.
Brad: I . . . can’t . . . blow . . . anymore!
Tina: I’m . . . out of . . . breath . . . too!
Danny: Don’t stop now, you guys!
Tina: Everybody blow!
Danny: Hurry!
Brad: Oh no!
Brad: That was close.
Tina: A little too close, if you ask me.
Danny: It looks like we’re stuck again. Now what are we going to do? We’ll never get to Ginormous from here.
Brad: Ginormous! What about getting home?
Danny: We can’t go home. You promised to help.
Brad: I didn’t know we would end up trapped on a cliff!
Tina: Oh, Brad! We need to help the giants. Imagine living in a world without color.
Brad: Sure, that would be terrible. But why is it my problem?
Danny: Because you can help, that’s why.
Brad: I guess you’re right.
Tina: Brad is right about one thing, though.
Danny: What’s that?
Tina: We are trapped on a cliff.
Danny: Wait a minute. I’ve got an idea.
Brad: What is it?
Danny: See? We can use these to climb back up to the top.
Tina: Great idea, Danny!
Brad: Wow, that’s a long way.
Tina: I didn’t realize we had fallen so far. I think it’s less scary if we climb down.
Danny: It does look shorter.
Brad: Either way, it’s not going to be easy.
Tina: Let’s go for it!
Danny: How are you guys doing?
Tina: Not bad. These suction cups work great.
Brad: It’s not as fun as the water slide, though.
Danny: I think the rock is wetter here.
Brad: It’s spray from the waterfall and the river. It means we’re getting closer to the bottom.
Tina: It shouldn’t be much farther.
Danny: I think my suction cups are slipping.
Brad: The rocks are too slippery. Mine are slipping too.
Tina: Let’s hurry up.
Danny: Faster, everyone!
Tina: Hold on!
Danny: We’re going to fall!
Brad: Oh no!
Brad: What are we going to do now!
Tina: I see a log up ahead. It’s sticking out from the riverbank.
Danny: I don’t think I can swim to it.
Tina: Just hold onto me. I’m a great swimmer. We’re almost there!
Danny: Good work, Tina.
Brad: Okay, what now?
Tina: Now we just have to crawl across to dry land over there. I’ll go first. Come on, guys! I’ll help you up!
Brad: We’d better hurry. This doesn’t feel very steady.
Danny: You first, Brad.
Tina: Okay. Come on, Danny!
Danny: We made it!
Brad: Yeah, but I don’t think my computer did.
Tina: Okay, now that we’re on dry land, what next?
Danny: We still need to find Hopian’s land.
Brad: But how?
Tina: What about trying the key again?
Danny: It’s not in great shape.
Brad: That looks more like mud than clay.
Tina: Try it anyway, Danny.
Danny: Open the door, open the door . . . It’s not working.
Brad: You do have other colors of clay, Danny.
Tina: Good idea, Brad! Try to make another key, Danny.
Danny Which color should I use?
Tina: Red. Because I’m wet and cold, and red reminds me of somewhere warm.

Danny: Well, the blue key did lead us to a land of water. I guess the red key might lead us somewhere warm. Okay, here goes . . . Done! Now I have to concentrate like last time. Ready? Take us to Ginormous, take us to Ginormous, take us to Ginormous. Is it working?
Tina: Not yet. Concentrate harder, Danny!
Brad: Danny is concentrating hard. I almost wish he takes us home.
Tina: Oh, Brad! We need to help the giants. Remember?
Brad: I know, I know. I’m just cold and tired. I don’t really mean it.
Tina: I know you don’t. I’m tired too.
Brad: Hey! Something’s happening!
Tina: Look, something is coming out of the ground!
Danny: It worked!
Tina: Way to go, Danny!
Brad: This door looks more inviting than the first door.
Danny: Let’s open it and find out!
Danny: Hello? Hopian?
Tina: Is anybody here?
Danny: Hopian? Hello!
Brad: I don’t know about this place . . . My computer is wet. I’m afraid it will freeze.
Tina: I’m more afraid that we’ll freeze!
Danny: Where’s Hopian?
Tina: Well, not right here. That’s for sure.
Brad: What should we do?
Tina: We need to do something to stay warm!
Danny: Let’s split up and look around.
Brad: Do you think that’s a good idea?
Tina: At least it will get us moving! We’re starting to freeze!
Danny: Let’s stay close enough that we can still hear each other. Tina, Brad, can you hear me?
Tina: Loud and clear!
Brad: You haven’t gone very far, Danny!
Danny: Just checking.
Brad: Do you guys know how cold it is in here?
Tina & Danny: Very?
Brad: It’s -20 degrees Celsius! We could freeze in here!
Brad: Hey guys?
Tina: Danny! Brad!
Danny: Tina, Brad! Where did you guys go!

Tina: Have you two found anything? I see piles of snow everywhere, but I can’t see what’s underneath them. I’m coming back to you now! Where are you guys? Hello? Guys! This isn’t funny. Fine, I can find you myself. I know you’re over here somewhere. Could one of you please say something? I’m getting scared. Danny? Brad? Oh no, Brad! You’re frozen! Brad, can you hear me?
